summary.text: William Colton is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to the New York State Assembly seat he has held since 1997.
A lawyer and former New York City public school teacher, he was active in Bensonhurst tenant and transit organizations before entering the Assembly.
Ballotpedia lists his committee assignments as Correction, Environmental Conservation, Governmental Employees, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Colton is a lifelong resident of the district, was educated at St. Athanasius School, and graduated from Cathedral Prep, the minor seminary of the Diocese of Brooklyn.
He earned a B.A. in Urban Education from St. John's University (1968), an M.S. in Urban Education from Brooklyn College, and a J.D. from St. John's University School of Law (1978).

He worked as a New York City public school teacher for eleven years, including six years as a UFT chapter chairperson, while attending law school in the evenings, and was admitted to practice law in New York in 1979.

Colton co-founded and organized the Bensonhurst Tenants Council, which worked to preserve apartment buildings in the neighborhood, and founded the Bensonhurst Straphangers Committee to advocate on transit issues.

His official biography also lists community work including serving as the attorney in a lawsuit to stop the re-opening of the Southwest Brooklyn Incinerator, and membership on boards of the Verrazano Lodge of the Order of the Sons of Italy and the Cardinal Stritch Knights Corporation of the Knights of Columbus.

Colton was first elected to the Assembly in November 1996 and has represented District 47 continuously since 1997; the district includes Bensonhurst, Gravesend, Bath Beach, Dyker Heights and Midwood, according to his official biography.
The same biography says he was appointed Chair of the Legislative Commission on Solid Waste Management.

His campaign website lists as accomplishments opposing the 2501 86th Street homeless shelter plan, fighting to keep the IS 228 schoolyard, and organizing neighborhood vaccine events during the COVID-19 pandemic.
